tabs.label: The city

paris.name: Tour Eiffel
paris.desc: Built for the 1889 World's Fair, on the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. It is 324 meters tall

paris.name: Arc de Triomphe
paris.desc: A monument dedicated to French victories. From its terrace, you can admire the great avenues of Paris

paris.name: Pyramide du Louvre
paris.desc: The Louvre's iconic entrance. Its glass structure contrasts with the palace's classical architecture

paris.name: Opéra Garnier
paris.desc: A magnificent 19th-century theater, with lavish decoration and an impressive marble staircase

paris.name: Conciergerie
paris.desc: A former royal palace turned into a prison during the Revolution. Marie Antoinette was imprisoned here

paris.name: Tour Montparnasse
paris.desc: A skyscraper with a panoramic terrace where you can take in Paris and the Eiffel Tower

paris.name: Panthéon
paris.desc: A neoclassical monument where great figures of French history rest, such as Victor Hugo and Marie Curie

paris.name: Odéon
paris.desc: A historic Parisian theater in the Latin Quarter, known for its shows and its elegant façade

paris.name: Hôtel des Invalides
paris.desc: A historic complex with a golden dome that houses Napoleon's tomb and the Army Museum

paris.name: Palais de la Porte Dorée
paris.desc: An Art Deco building that houses a museum of the history of immigration and a tropical aquarium

paris.name: Obélisque de Louxor
paris.desc: An Egyptian monument over 3,000 years old, standing on Place de la Concorde since 1836.

paris.name: Colonne de juillet
paris.desc: This column commemorates the July Revolution of 1830 and stands on the site of the former Bastille prison

paris.name: Colonne Vendôme
paris.desc: A monumental Roman-style column, built to celebrate Napoleon's victories

paris.name: Pont des arts
paris.desc: A bridge once famous for the padlocks couples attached to it as a symbol of love.

paris.name: Pont Alexandre III
paris.desc: One of the most elegant bridges in Paris, famous for its golden statues and ornate lampposts

paris.name: Pont Neuf
paris.desc: Despite its name (new bridge), it's the oldest bridge still standing in Paris. It offers lovely river views

paris.name: Grande Arche de la Défense
paris.desc: An impressive piece of modern architecture overlooking the La Défense business district

paris.name: Hôtel de la Marine
paris.desc: An elegant 18th-century palace on Place de la Concorde, with restored historic interiors

paris.name: Porte de Saint-Denis
paris.desc: A triumphal arch from 1672, built by order of Louis XIV to celebrate his military victories

paris.name: Statue de la Liberté
paris.desc: Paris has several replicas of the Statue of Liberty. The most famous one stands on the Île aux Cygnes

paris.name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris
paris.desc: One of the most famous cathedrals in the world, on the Île de la Cité, in the historic heart of Paris

paris.name: Sainte-Chapelle
paris.desc: A 13th-century royal chapel known for its huge stained-glass windows that fill the interior with light.

paris.name: Basilique du Sacré-Coeur
paris.desc: A white basilica at the top of Montmartre, famous for its panoramic views of Paris.

credit.author: Leonhard Niederwimmer – Lic. de contenido Pixabay

paris.name: Basilique Saint-Denis
paris.desc: An impressive Gothic basilica north of Paris, home to the tombs of many kings and queens of France

paris.name: Église de la Madeleine
paris.desc: A monumental church that looks like a Greek temple, surrounded by tall Corinthian columns.

paris.name: Grande Mosquée de Paris
paris.desc: Opened in 1926 to honor the Muslim soldiers who died for France in the Great War.

paris.name: Église Saint-Sulpice
paris.desc: A large church in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, famous for its organ and for appearing in The Da Vinci Code.

paris.name: Synagogue de la Victoire
paris.desc: The Great Synagogue of Paris is a monumental 19th-century building on Rue de la Victoire.

paris.name: Grande Pagode de Vincennes
paris.desc: A Buddhist temple surrounded by greenery, in the Bois de Vincennes.

paris.name: Chapelle expiatoire
paris.desc: A memorial chapel surrounded by gardens, built in memory of Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette.

paris.name: Cimetière du Père-Lachaise
paris.desc: A huge cemetery where figures like Édith Piaf and Frédéric Chopin rest.

paris.name: Catacombes de Paris
paris.desc: An underground maze holding the remains of millions of Parisians moved from old cemeteries.

paris.name: Paroisse Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis
paris.desc: An elegant Baroque church in the Marais, recognizable by its grand façade and its dome.

paris.name: Église Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois
paris.desc: A historic church facing the Louvre, mixing Gothic and Renaissance styles.

paris.name: Église Saint-Séverin
paris.desc: A Gothic church in the Latin Quarter, known for its vaults, its stained glass and its peaceful atmosphere.

paris.name: Église Saint-Eustache
paris.desc: A church where Mozart's mother's funeral was held (1778).

paris.name: Église Saint-Germain-des-prés
paris.desc: One of the oldest churches in Paris, in a neighborhood known for its cafés, bookshops and intellectual life

paris.name: Église Saint-Étienne-du-Mont
paris.desc: A Gothic and Renaissance church where Saint Geneviève, patron saint of Paris, is buried

paris.name: Église Saint-Roch
paris.desc: The building was damaged during the French Revolution — you can still see bullet marks

paris.name: Cimetière du Montparnasse
paris.desc: Home to the graves of Simone de Beauvoir, Jean-Paul Sartre and Serge Gainsbourg.

paris.name: Musée du Louvre
paris.desc: Discover masterpieces like the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo and the Winged Victory of Samothrace

paris.name: Musée d'Orsay
paris.desc: Admire Impressionist paintings by Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh and Degas in a former train station.

paris.name: Centre Pompidou
paris.desc: A landmark of modern and contemporary art, with architecture famous for its colorful pipes.

paris.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
paris.desc: Immerse yourself in Monet's "Water Lilies" and discover works by Renoir, Cézanne, Matisse and Picasso.

paris.name: Musée du Quai Branly
paris.desc: Explore the cultures and arts of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas through objects, sculptures and masks

paris.name: Musée Rodin
paris.desc: See Auguste Rodin's sculptures, including The Thinker, and stroll through a garden full of artworks.

paris.name: Petit Palais
paris.desc: Collections of painting, sculpture and decorative arts from Antiquity to the early 20th century

paris.name: Musée Carnavalet
paris.desc: Travel through the history of Paris from Antiquity to today through paintings and everyday objects…

paris.name: Maison de Victor Hugo
paris.desc: Visit the apartment where writer Victor Hugo lived and discover his belongings, manuscripts and drawings…

paris.name: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris
paris.desc: Located in the Palais de Tokyo, discover 20th- and 21st-century art

paris.name: Palais de Tokyo
paris.desc: Discover bold contemporary art exhibitions, installations and experimental works

paris.name: Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
paris.desc: See animals from all over the world and discover how life on Earth has evolved

paris.name: Fondation Louis Vuitton
paris.desc: Enjoy modern art exhibitions in a cutting-edge glass building designed by Frank Gehry

paris.name: Institut du monde arabe
paris.desc: Explore the history, art and cultures of the Arab world through objects and exhibitions

paris.name: Musée de Cluny
paris.desc: Step into the Middle Ages through tapestries, sculptures, stained glass and historic objects.

paris.name: Musée des Arts et Métiers
paris.desc: Discover inventions, machines, scientific instruments and technological breakthroughs that shaped history

paris.name: Musée Grévin
paris.desc: Take photos with wax figures of celebrities, historical figures, athletes and artists

paris.name: Musée Guimet
paris.desc: Admire a major collection of Asian art, with Buddhist sculptures, ceramics, textiles and objects.

paris.name: Musée Marmottan Monet
paris.desc: Immerse yourself in Claude Monet's world and see Impressionist paintings by other artists of the movement.

paris.name: Cité de l'Architecture et du Patrimoine
paris.desc: Discover French architecture from the Middle Ages to today, with sculptures, paintings and models.

paris.name: Château de Versailles
paris.desc: Discover the residence of the kings of France, with its lavish halls, the Hall of Mirrors and its gardens.

paris.name: Château de Fontainebleau
paris.desc: Explore a residence lived in for centuries by kings and emperors, with royal apartments

paris.name: Provins (Medieval town)
paris.desc: Travel back to the Middle Ages in this fortified town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site

paris.name: Château de Vaux-le-Vicomte
paris.desc: Admire an elegant 17th-century château. Its architecture inspired the creation of Versailles.

paris.name: Château de Chantilly
paris.desc: Explore a château that houses a major collection of old master paintings and magnificent gardens.

paris.name: Château de Rambouillet
paris.desc: Discover a former royal and presidential residence, famous for the Queen's Dairy.

paris.name: Domaine de Sceaux
paris.desc: Stroll through a vast French park with canals, fountains and gardens designed by Le Nôtre.

paris.name: Château de Vincennes
paris.desc: Discover a medieval fortress with ramparts, towers and an imposing keep over 50 meters tall.

paris.name: Château de Maisons-Laffitte
paris.desc: Discover a gem of 17th-century French classical architecture, with a grand staircase and elegant salons.

paris.name: Château Vieux de Saint- Germain-en-Laye
paris.desc: A former residence of the kings of France, this château now houses the National Archaeology Museum.

paris.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
paris.desc: Walk through flower gardens, or relax by the pond where children sail little toy boats

paris.name: Jardin des Tuileries
paris.desc: Enjoy a classic garden between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde, with green chairs to relax in.

paris.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
paris.desc: A park with hills, waterfalls and a temple on a cliff. Its artificial landscape was created in the 19th century.

paris.name: Parc Monceau
paris.desc: An elegant garden with century-old trees, sculptures, a pond and a charming rotunda.

paris.name: Jardin des Plantes
paris.desc: Discover botanical gardens, greenhouses and remarkable trees. It was created in 1626 as a royal medicinal garden.

paris.name: Parc de la Villette
paris.desc: A large cultural green space, home to the famous Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie.

paris.name: Bois de Boulogne
paris.desc: A huge forest west of Paris, with lakes, trails, waterfalls, gardens and the Parc de Bagatelle

paris.name: Bois de Vincennes
paris.desc: The great green lung of eastern Paris, with lakes, woods, trails, a zoo and the Parc Floral.

paris.name: Parc floral de Paris
paris.desc: A botanical garden with flower collections, themed plants, sculptures and play areas.

paris.name: Parc Montsouris
paris.desc: A peaceful landscaped park with a lake, lawns, century-old trees and many sculptures.

paris.name: Parc de Bercy
paris.desc: A garden built in the old wine-warehouse district, with vegetable gardens, themed gardens and trails.

paris.name: Jardin du Palais-Royal
paris.desc: A quiet garden; in the entrance courtyard you'll find Buren's famous contemporary columns.

paris.name: Champs-de-Mars
paris.desc: A large park at the foot of the Eiffel Tower, perfect for a picnic while admiring the iron giant.

credit.author: Diliff, edited by Fir0002– CC BY-SA 2.5

paris.name: Jardin du Trocadéro
paris.desc: Enjoy the most iconic view of the Eiffel Tower, with terraces and steps leading down to the Seine.

paris.name: Parc de Belleville
paris.desc: A hillside park in eastern Paris, with terraced gardens and a beautiful view over the city's rooftops.

paris.name: Esplanade des Invalides
paris.desc: A wide green esplanade leading to the Hôtel des Invalides and its golden dome.

paris.name: Place des Vosges
paris.desc: An elegant garden square, considered one of the oldest planned squares in Paris.

paris.name: Jardin des Serres d'Auteuil
paris.desc: A botanical garden with historic greenhouses, tropical plants and species from all over the world

paris.name: Parc André-Citroën
paris.desc: A park on the banks of the Seine, known for its themed gardens, its greenhouses and its big hot-air balloon

paris.name: Arènes de Lutèce
paris.desc: Discover the remains of a Gallo-Roman amphitheater where shows were held nearly 2,000 years ago.

paris.name: Champs-Élysées
paris.desc: Walk along the famous Parisian avenue, lined with shops, cafés and grand buildings, and listen to this song

paris.name: Montmartre
paris.desc: Stroll its cobbled streets and discover its artists and little cafés. The famous neighborhood of "La Bohème"

paris.name: Le Marais
paris.desc: Get lost in its historic streets and discover elegant mansions, independent boutiques, galleries and cafés.

paris.name: Quartier Latin
paris.desc: Visit one of the oldest neighborhoods in Paris, famous for its universities, bookshops, restaurants and streets.

paris.name: Cour Saint-Émilion
paris.desc: Discover a pedestrian area full of restaurants and terraces set up in former wine warehouses.

paris.name: Quai de Seine
paris.desc: Walk along the Seine, admire the historic bridges and discover the green stalls of the "bouquinistes".

paris.name: Canal Saint-Martin
paris.desc: Enjoy a waterside walk among iron footbridges, locks, cafés and little boutiques.

paris.name: Île de la cité
paris.desc: Explore the historic heart of Paris. The island still bears traces of the city's Roman and medieval origins

paris.name: Île Saint-Louis
paris.desc: Enjoy a peaceful walk among 17th-century façades, elegant mansions, little shops and ice-cream parlors

paris.name: Châtelet
paris.desc: Explore a central area with squares, theaters, shops and shopping streets. A major transport hub

paris.name: Belleville
paris.desc: Explore a multicultural neighborhood known for its street art and its restaurants from all over the world

paris.name: Galeries Lafayette Haussmann
paris.desc: Go up to the rooftop of the Galeries Lafayette department store for a panoramic view of Paris

paris.name: Rue Mouffetard
paris.desc: Walk one of the most picturesque streets in the Latin Quarter, with food stalls, bakeries and markets

paris.name: Galerie Vivienne
paris.desc: One of the most elegant covered passages in Paris, famous for its mosaic floor and its glass roof

paris.name: La Défense
paris.desc: Discover the big business district of Paris, with skyscrapers and a huge pedestrian esplanade

paris.name: Quartier François Mitterrand
paris.desc: Discover a modern Paris around the National Library of France, right by the Seine

paris.name: Coulée verte René-Dumont
paris.desc: Walk along an elevated garden built on an old railway line. This green corridor crosses the 12th district

paris.name: Rue Crémieux
paris.desc: Discover a small pedestrian street with pastel-colored façades. It's very popular for photos

paris.name: Place de la République
paris.desc: The square is home to the statue of Marianne, symbol of the Republic. It's an iconic spot for protests.

paris.name: Pigalle
paris.desc: Discover a neighborhood known for its nightlife, with its bars, concert halls and cabarets (Moulin Rouge)

paris.name: Disneyland Paris
paris.desc: Two theme parks with rides, parades, shows and meet-and-greets with Disney characters.

paris.name: Bateaux-Mouches
paris.desc: Discover Paris along the Seine and admire its monuments on a boat ride.

paris.name: Moulin Rouge
paris.desc: The famous Parisian cabaret with the red windmill, known for its music, dance and feather shows.

paris.name: Atelier des Lumières
paris.desc: An immersive art center where monumental paintings and images are projected onto the walls

paris.name: Cité des Sciences
paris.desc: A large interactive science museum with activities for all ages.

paris.name: Zoo de Vincennes
paris.desc: A zoo where you can discover animals and ecosystems from different regions of the world

paris.name: Aquarium de Paris
paris.desc: An aquarium where you can see sharks, jellyfish and many aquatic animals in huge tanks.

paris.name: Parc d'Acclimatation
paris.desc: A leisure park with rides, games, gardens and activities to enjoy with kids.

paris.name: Folies Bergère
paris.desc: A historic theater hosting musicals, concerts, comedies and other shows

paris.name: Le Grand Rex
paris.desc: An iconic movie theater with a spectacular giant screen. It also offers events and behind-the-scenes tours.

paris.name: Cirque d'Hiver Bouglione
paris.desc: A historic circus in an elegant building, with shows combining acrobatics and circus arts

paris.name: Aquaboulevard
paris.desc: A large water park with pools, waves and slides, perfect for a few hours of fun and cooling off.

paris.name: Parc des Princes
paris.desc: Paris Saint-Germain's stadium. You can visit during matches and, depending on availability, on guided tours

paris.name: iFly Paris
paris.desc: An indoor skydiving experience: a powerful wind tunnel lets you float in the air

paris.name: Musée de l'Illusion
paris.desc: An interactive museum of optical illusions, perspective tricks and visual experiences

paris.name: Barques à Vincennes
paris.desc: Rent a rowboat on Lake Daumesnil and enjoy a peaceful ride

paris.name: Roue de Paris (Nov – Feb)
paris.desc: Enjoy a panoramic view of Paris from this big Ferris wheel, usually next to the Tuileries Garden.

cards.title: Districts
cards.text: Numbered in a spiral, from the center outward. In French, they're called:

cards.title: banks
cards.text: The Right Bank, to the north, and the Left Bank, to the south of the Seine

transport: Gets you around the whole city and the nearby suburbs
Crosses Paris and reaches the suburbs. It connects to the metro and can take you to Disney, the Palace of Versailles or both Paris airports
The tram runs around the edge of Paris

security.title: Watch out for pickpockets!
security.text: Especially in the metro and in very touristy areas
chips: Be wary of strangers in the street
Phone hidden, not on the table
Beware of requests and fake charity collections

hours: Many shops close on Sundays (except in December).
In restaurants, lunch is served around 12–2 pm, and dinner from 7 pm.
Museums close on Monday or Tuesday
The first metro leaves around 5:30 am and the last one reaches the end of the line around 1:15 am, and around 2:15 am on Friday and Saturday nights.
